onboarding.story.1.a: Sweet Home began in a small rented room in Korea.
onboarding.story.1.b: A student far from home: classes by day, a part-time job at night. By the time they got back to the room, everyone at home was asleep.
onboarding.story.2.a: They missed Mom and Dad so much. But every time they called, all they could say was “I'm fine.”
onboarding.story.2.b: They couldn't do much for the family yet, so they felt shy about sharing their own days.
onboarding.story.3.a: Back home, Mom and Dad felt the same. They missed their child, but were afraid that asking too much would only worry them.
onboarding.story.3.b: Two ends of one longing, and each side kept it to themselves.
onboarding.story.4.a: Then one day they thought: what if a letter went home every week?
onboarding.story.4.b: It doesn't have to be long. A photo, a question, a voice.
onboarding.story.5.b: For you, and for the people waiting for you at home.
onboarding.role.q: Who are you in the family?
onboarding.kid.q.parent: Is your child a boy or a girl?
onboarding.kid.q.child: Are you a son or a daughter to Mom and Dad?
onboarding.name.q: What does everyone at home call you?
onboarding.dob.sub.parent: So your kids never forget this day.
onboarding.dob.sub.child: So Mom and Dad remember to wish you well.
onboarding.city.sub: So everyone knows the time and weather over there.
onboarding.seen.q.parent: How long has it been since you saw your child?
onboarding.seen.q.child: How long has it been since you were home?
onboarding.seen.echo.week: So the hugs are still warm.
onboarding.seen.echo.months: A few months is plenty of time for stories to pile up.
onboarding.seen.echo.year.parent: Over a year. They must be counting the days until they're home.
onboarding.seen.echo.year.child: Over a year. Home has probably seen a few Lunar New Years without you.
onboarding.seen.echo.together: Close, yet far. Let's start again with one small question.
onboarding.hug.q.parent: Would you like to hug {kids} right now?
onboarding.hug.q.child: Would you like to hug Mom and Dad right now?
onboarding.hug.echo.yes.parent: Then give {kids} a big, tight hug in a little while.
onboarding.hug.echo.yes.child: Then give Mom and Dad a big, tight hug in a little while.
onboarding.hug.echo.no.parent: That's okay. Whenever you miss {kids}, we'll hug later.
onboarding.hug.echo.no.child: That's okay. Whenever you miss home, we'll hug later.
onboarding.food.q.parent: Do you remember what your child loves to eat?
onboarding.food.q.child: What food from home do you miss most?
onboarding.food.echo.parent: That dish, they probably still remember the taste.
onboarding.food.echo.child: Next time you call home, ask Mom how she makes it.
onboarding.love.q.parent: Have you ever told your child “I love you”?
onboarding.love.q.child: Have you ever told Mom and Dad “I love you”?
onboarding.love.echo.sometimes.parent: Even now and then is enough to keep a whole week warm.
onboarding.love.echo.never.parent: Parents often love without saying it. Your child knows anyway.
onboarding.love.echo.often.child: Mom and Dad must be so happy every time they hear it.
onboarding.love.echo.sometimes.child: Next time, say it one more time.
onboarding.love.echo.never.child: That's okay. Some words take time. Sweet Home will help.
onboarding.voice.q.parent: Say just one sentence, right now.
onboarding.voice.q.child: Say just one sentence, right now.
onboarding.voice.sub.child: Something like: “I love you, Mom and Dad.”
onboarding.voice.kept: That sentence will be the first letter in your home.
onboarding.voice.denied: The mic isn't allowed yet. No problem, we'll talk later.
onboarding.unsaid.q.parent: Is there something you want to tell your child but haven't?
onboarding.unsaid.q.child: Is there something you want to tell Mom and Dad but haven't?
onboarding.unsaid.echo.parent: Sweet Home will keep it until the right moment for them to hear it.
onboarding.unsaid.echo.child: Some things are hard to say out loud. Sweet Home will keep it for you.
onboarding.unsaid.placeholder: Write here, only you can see it
